metadata.title: PROJECT ATLAS — Keplerian Orbital Elements & Belt Regions
metadata.primarySource: NASA NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheets & Solar System Facts
metadata.disclaimer: Educational simplified Keplerian orbital model initialized from J2000 mean elements. Does not provide mission-grade N-body ephemerides or precision spacecraft navigation.

beltRegions.name: Main Asteroid Belt
beltRegions.description: A torus-shaped region between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter populated by rocky remnants from the early Solar System ~4.6 billion years ago. Jupiter's strong gravitational perturbations prevented these planetesimals from accreting into a single planet. Ceres alone accounts for ~25% of the belt's total mass.
beltRegions.visualizationNote: Rendered using GPU-efficient Three.js InstancedMesh; density is compressed for visibility as real asteroids are separated by millions of kilometers.

beltRegions.name: Kuiper Belt
beltRegions.rangeAU: 30 – 50 AU (Beyond Neptune's orbit, with scattered disk extending farther)
beltRegions.description: A vast doughnut-shaped region of icy worlds and trans-Neptunian objects (KBOs) beyond the orbit of Neptune. Formed ~4.5 billion years ago, it holds thousands of icy bodies and is the source of many short-period comets.
beltRegions.visualizationNote: Rendered via instanced icy bodies plus interactive 3D orbits for Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris.

beltRegions.name: Oort Cloud (Conceptual Shell)
beltRegions.rangeAU: 5,000 – 100,000 AU (Boundary of the Sun's gravitational influence)
representativeObjects: Long-Period Comets (Conceptual reservoir; no individual Oort Cloud objects are directly mapped in situ)
beltRegions.description: A theoretical, thick spherical shell of icy planetesimals surrounding the Solar System from roughly 5,000 AU to 100,000 AU. It marks the outer boundary of the Sun's gravitational dominance. While Voyager 1 and 2 crossed the heliosphere's termination shock (80–100 AU), it will take thousands of years for them to traverse the Oort Cloud.
beltRegions.visualizationNote: CONCEPTUAL VISUALIZATION ONLY: Individual Oort Cloud objects are not directly mapped, and its exact outer boundary is not precisely known.
